entries.rationale: A closed set of low-risk browser prototype shapes covers the fixed template while preventing an unreviewed general coding surface.
One primary persona keeps the outcome and acceptance criteria bounded enough for a five-screen prototype.
The MVP value unit explicitly proves one primary user flow and requires a founder-authored narrowing decision for more.
Five routes is the authoritative MVP ceiling and matches the accepted fixed-template architecture.
The first alpha evaluates responsive browser prototypes and explicitly excludes native, desktop, and extension output.
The accepted sandbox decision permits one checksum-verified React and TypeScript template rather than arbitrary project stacks.
Client-only behavior prevents generated backends, production actions, credentials, and external business effects in the MVP.
Local mock data supports demonstrations without customer, sensitive, credential, payment, or production-system data.
This closed denial registry converts authoritative MVP non-goals into deterministic qualification results without silently dropping requested behavior.
Five focused questions is the SRS ceiling and avoids turning qualification into an unbounded conversation.
Plain text, Markdown, PDF, PNG, JPEG, and WebP cover necessary references while excluding active and executable document classes.
Five references provide useful product context while bounding scan, extraction, prompt, storage, and review load.
Per-type byte ceilings bound parser and scanner exposure while allowing ordinary short documents and reference imagery.
A twenty MiB aggregate ceiling prevents multiple individually valid files from bypassing the run storage and processing budget.
Fifty pages is enough for bounded product references without accepting long-document ingestion or unbounded extraction work.
A twenty-megapixel decoded-image ceiling prevents decompression abuse while retaining useful interface and visual references.
Every attachment must pass type, integrity, safety, parser, and tenant checks before promotion or use by any employee or tool.
Active, nested, ambiguous, encrypted, and executable formats exceed the safe reference-only attachment boundary for private alpha.
Failures that invalidate approved behavior, build integrity, safety, isolation, the primary flow, or required evidence cannot reach final-ready state.
Advisory findings remain visible without consuming rework when the approved flow, evidence, security, and build gates still pass.
Each rework reruns affected evidence plus a fixed safety and build regression set so a local repair cannot silently break accepted behavior.
A narrow mobile browser width and a desktop width provide a deterministic minimum responsive check for every primary screen and state.
Critical and serious automated accessibility findings block final readiness while lesser findings remain visible and measured during alpha.
A thirty-two Ki-token input ceiling bounds context assembly and reservation size before any provider dispatch.
An eight Ki-token output ceiling is sufficient for typed artifacts while bounding validation, repair, latency, and cost.
The run-level input ceiling permits the fixed workflow and two rework cycles without allowing an unbounded conversation or context loop.
The run-level output ceiling bounds cumulative artifacts, retries, and repairs while leaving headroom for the fixed employee sequence.
A two dollar and fifty cent reservation ceiling prevents one call from consuming the conservative run safety allowance.
A fifteen dollar hard safety ceiling limits alpha exposure but is not the deferred acceptable per-completed-run economic target.
A two-minute hard invocation deadline bounds latency and leaves post-dispatch uncertainty to explicit reconciliation rather than replay.
Twenty-four invocations cover fixed stages, bounded repair, and two rework cycles while making accidental agent loops finite.
R0 remains deterministic-fixture-only until a separate exact provider, account, terms, retention, disclosure, and spend manifest is accepted.
Ninety minutes of system-active time bounds a run near the MVP sixty-minute median target while excluding persisted founder waits.
Five minutes per allowlisted command supports the fixed build while preventing hung or adversarial processes from running indefinitely.
Thirty minutes of aggregate sandbox wall time bounds builds and rework inside the ninety-minute active-run ceiling.
Two CPU cores are sufficient for the pinned frontend toolchain and keep concurrent private-alpha resource demand predictable.
Forty CPU-minutes permit bounded compilation and tests while limiting busy-loop consumption below the aggregate wall and core product.
Two GiB supports the fixed React and TypeScript build without granting unbounded host memory to generated code.
A 128-process ceiling supports package tooling while preventing fork bombs and runaway process trees.
A 512 MiB writable ceiling contains temporary build expansion while dependency layers remain read-only and platform managed.
Five thousand writable files cover generated source and build intermediates without permitting uncontrolled filesystem fan-out.
A one MiB source-file ceiling prevents generated blobs and logs from masquerading as maintainable text source.
A twenty-five MiB source snapshot is ample for five client routes while excluding dependency caches and binary bulk.
A one-hundred MiB build-output ceiling accommodates the fixed static bundle while bounding preview and export materialization.
One MiB of captured output per command preserves actionable diagnostics without allowing unbounded or content-bearing logs.
Ten MiB of redacted retained logs bounds storage and disclosure while preserving structured evidence for a failed run.
A 256 MiB run ceiling contains attachments, source, build output, artifacts, and bounded evidence without setting retention duration.
One persisted transient retry limits cost and delay while preserving a deterministic attempt and evidence boundary.
One separately reserved schema repair matches the accepted provider contract and prevents self-amplifying repair loops.
Three recorded task attempts bound initial work, one eligible retry, and one replacement path without hiding each outcome.
Provider SDK retries remain disabled so every invocation, reservation, timeout, and outcome is visible to the durable runtime.
Build commands do not repeat automatically; a new attempt requires a classified durable decision and fresh budget reservation.
Unknown post-dispatch outcomes block for reconciliation and are never automatically replayed as though no effect occurred.
Two automatic Engineer and QA rework cycles are an authoritative MVP boundary and stop further automatic cost expansion.
The invite-only cohort is capped at five founders so support, cost, and incident response remain attributable during alpha.
One active run per company matches the Prototype Initiative invariant and prevents self-contention and ambiguous founder decisions.
Two globally active runs provide limited overlap while keeping the small-team worker, storage, and support surface observable.
One active isolated build prevents host oversubscription until sandbox measurements demonstrate safe parallel capacity.
Two concurrent model invocations match the active-run ceiling and bound quota, spend, cancellation, and rate-limit pressure.
The SRS requires a capacity test at approved alpha concurrency plus a two-times safety factor before launch.
Four active test runs prove the two-run alpha ceiling at the required two-times safety factor.
Two active test builds prove the single-build alpha ceiling at the required two-times safety factor.
Four concurrent fixture invocations prove the two-invocation alpha ceiling at the required two-times safety factor.

reason_codes.founder_message: This prototype category is not enabled for the private alpha.
reason_codes.next_action: Choose an eligible category or submit a new, narrower goal version.

reason_codes.founder_message: The goal contains more than one primary persona.
reason_codes.next_action: Choose one primary persona and submit a new goal version.

reason_codes.founder_message: The goal contains more than one primary user flow.
reason_codes.next_action: Choose one flow to prototype and submit a new goal version.

reason_codes.founder_message: The proposed flow needs more than five screens or routes.
reason_codes.next_action: Narrow the flow to five screens or fewer and submit a new goal version.

reason_codes.founder_message: The requested output is not a responsive browser prototype.
reason_codes.next_action: Reframe the goal as a responsive web flow or cancel this initiative.

reason_codes.founder_message: The requested stack does not fit the fixed private-alpha template.
reason_codes.next_action: Accept the fixed React and TypeScript template or narrow the goal.

reason_codes.founder_message: The requested behavior requires a generated backend or production service.
reason_codes.next_action: Replace it with a client-side mock interaction and submit a new goal version.

reason_codes.founder_message: The requested behavior requires real, sensitive, or external data.
reason_codes.next_action: Use safe local mock data and submit a new goal version.

reason_codes.founder_message: The goal requests a capability outside the private-alpha boundary.
reason_codes.next_action: Review the cited limitation, remove that capability, and submit a new goal version.

reason_codes.founder_message: The goal is missing information required to qualify the primary flow.
reason_codes.next_action: Answer the bounded clarification questions or cancel the initiative.

reason_codes.founder_message: An attachment type is not allowed for private alpha.
reason_codes.next_action: Upload plain text, Markdown, PDF, PNG, JPEG, or WebP instead.

reason_codes.founder_message: The goal includes more than five attachments.
reason_codes.next_action: Remove extra references and resubmit the goal version.

reason_codes.founder_message: An attachment exceeds its allowed file-size limit.
reason_codes.next_action: Reduce or replace the file and submit it again.

reason_codes.founder_message: The combined attachments exceed the twenty MiB run limit.
reason_codes.next_action: Remove or reduce attachments and submit them again.

reason_codes.founder_message: A PDF contains more than fifty pages.
reason_codes.next_action: Provide a shorter excerpt that contains only the necessary reference pages.

reason_codes.founder_message: An image exceeds the decoded-pixel safety limit.
reason_codes.next_action: Resize the image below twenty megapixels and upload it again.

reason_codes.founder_message: An attachment could not be safely validated.
reason_codes.next_action: Replace the file with a clean supported reference and try again.

reason_codes.founder_message: An attachment contains an unsupported or unsafe content class.
reason_codes.next_action: Remove active, encrypted, nested, or executable content and provide a safe reference.

reason_codes.founder_message: A required quality or safety check did not pass.
reason_codes.next_action: Review the linked finding and wait for bounded rework or choose a founder action.

reason_codes.founder_message: QA found a non-blocking improvement opportunity.
reason_codes.next_action: Review the advisory finding; it does not prevent the current final decision.

reason_codes.founder_message: A change requires affected checks and the fixed regression set to run again.
reason_codes.next_action: Wait for the new QA evidence before making the final decision.

reason_codes.founder_message: The prototype failed a required narrow or desktop viewport check.
reason_codes.next_action: Review the affected screen and wait for bounded rework.

reason_codes.founder_message: A critical or serious automated accessibility issue remains.
reason_codes.next_action: Review the finding and wait for bounded rework before final approval.

reason_codes.founder_message: The current model invocation reached a hard time, token, or cost limit.
reason_codes.next_action: Review the blocker; no additional model work will start without an eligible recovery action.

reason_codes.founder_message: The run reached a hard token, cost, storage, output, or invocation limit.
reason_codes.next_action: Review the budget summary and choose an available recovery or cancellation action.

reason_codes.founder_message: The run reached its hard active-execution time limit.
reason_codes.next_action: Review the persisted blocker and choose an available recovery or cancellation action.

reason_codes.founder_message: The isolated build reached a hard resource or output limit.
reason_codes.next_action: Review the bounded build evidence; unsafe or late output was not accepted.

reason_codes.founder_message: The allowed retry or repair attempts are exhausted.
reason_codes.next_action: Review the last classified failure and choose an available founder action.

reason_codes.founder_message: The two automatic QA rework cycles are exhausted.
reason_codes.next_action: Review the remaining findings and choose a bounded founder decision.

reason_codes.founder_message: Private-alpha execution capacity is currently full.
reason_codes.next_action: Keep the run queued without side effects or try again after capacity is available.

reason_codes.founder_message: The private-alpha founder cohort is currently full.
reason_codes.next_action: Remain on the waitlist until an explicitly approved cohort slot is available.

reason_codes.founder_message: External model execution is not enabled for this policy version.
reason_codes.next_action: Use deterministic internal fixtures only; wait for a separately accepted provider configuration.
